title: Property income still a core focus
full_text:
A legal specialist has stated the high concentration of property as investment assets across the SMSF sector means the ATO will continue to look more closely at income and deductions derived from them.
DBA Lawyers principal Dan Butler said the ATO has flagged that nine out of 10 tax returns lodged reported rental income that was incorrect and the intersection with superannuation rules that occurs with SMSFs created further complexity for taxpayers.
“There is probably a higher risk in the SMSF territory of things getting wrong than outside of it when you see the total value of property investments,” Butler said during a presentation at the recent Tax Institute National Superannuation Conference in Melbourne.
“It is hard to really calibrate, but I took a bit of a stab at it and estimate that 21 per cent of total SMSF assets could be, in one way or another, linked to property, even though it is hard to get an accurate figure based on the ATO statistics.
“So what the regulator is looking at is has your fund reported its income correctly.
“Some people pick net rental income rather than go to the real estate agent statement who says: ‘Here’s your gross rent and this is where we have taken out these expenses.’
“Have you claimed the right deductions? Remember the repair versus improvement question where you have a leaking roof and you have to replace it, but we now use modern-day materials and you can’t just replace it as it was.
“You have to do things which could be considered improvements and that gets into the hardball decisions of making these calls.
“You will need to go through the [ATO’s] rulings and case law to justify your position and note it on file as the approach you’re taking.
“At times you may want to go to the supplier and say: ‘You’re the expert. Tell us what is a repair versus an improvement based on current protocols.’
“You don’t have to make the call, but your clients as taxpayers have to. They’re ultimately responsible, but as an agent or adviser, you need to be able to give them the evidence to support their position.”
author: Jason Spits
